title: RAW UNREVIEWED: shared head term with different plant-specific processing
summary: GDT1090's schor match holds only for one retrospectively selected image-code union, so it cannot name an organ. Search an admitted pair of visually distinct Herbal owners with independently sourced, different uses of the same explicitly named reproductive part. Freeze each source's part, action, input and output before reading both complete Voynich paragraphs. A candidate common term must keep the part role while the owner-specific operations differ in the predicted direction; a generic entry formula or whole-plant term is a live rival. Require a second owner with a source-written action contrast and a prospectively licensed text-to-part pointer before selection. No such eligible pair or word meaning is asserted here.

design.mechanism: a reusable part noun is invariant while complete source-owned processing relations change across distinct plants
design.unit: two independently identified historical plant entries and their two complete admitted Voynich records
design.contrast: shared reproductive-part referent with opposite or distinct preparation actions versus generic entry formula or plant-name recurrence
design.prediction: the frozen whole readings preserve the same part role and recover both owner-specific actions and outputs; absent a prospective owner pointer means missing capacity
